1.name: Alfred Jones
lines: Hi, I'm Alfred Jones: 52, a widower, and worth about $1,000,000, not counting my house.
Trouble is, it's scattered across 11 institutions, in bonds, stocks, GICs and mutual funds.
I research constantly and only get more confused. My advisers toss me ideas, but nobody gives me a direction.
I want a comfortable retirement and a real legacy for my two kids. Can you pull it all into one plan?
1.mission: Clear Stage 1 to turn Alfred's scattered accounts into one real financial plan.
1.debrief: Thanks! One planner, one plan: goals in real numbers, a full view of my assets, then loss control and loss financing.

2.name: Alfred Jones
lines: Alfred again. Time to look at what could go wrong, starting with my $400,000 house and $200,000 cottage.
Add $20,000 of art, $10,000 in coins, and $85,000 of cars, my vintage Mustang among them.
I'm a self-employed consulting engineer. If I fall ill, most of my income dries up, and so could retiring at 60.
And I've booked a month in Hawaii: golf, scuba, beach! Help me spot every risk before it strikes.
2.mission: Clear Stage 2 to expose every peril and hazard stalking Alfred.
2.debrief: Thanks! Personal, property, liability, travel: once my risks are measured, we can manage them, insurance included.

3.name: Alfred Jones
lines: Insurance? Bah! Term just eats your premiums, and most folks never collect a dime.
Cash value policies? Investments are what I care about, and I doubt those pay a decent return.
My bank deposits have CDIC coverage. If an insurance company goes under, what protects me?
And how do I know an agent's advice is honest and independent? Convince me this industry is safe!
3.mission: Clear Stage 3 to show skeptical Alfred the insurance industry is solid and regulated.
3.debrief: Thanks! Only three Canadian life insurers failed in 100-plus years, Assuris protects me, and agents are licensed.

4.name: Sean
lines: Hi, I'm Sean, Alfred's son: 24 and just out of university.
A guy in a bar kept the drinks coming, and I signed up for a $250,000 whole life policy. I can't afford it!
Dad's got questions too: an outdated beneficiary, a $5,000 stereo, and what all-perils really covers.
Am I stuck with this contract? Help us read the fine print!
4.mission: Clear Stage 4 to rescue Sean from a barroom policy and decode the fine print.
4.debrief: Thanks! The 10-day free look lets me cancel, and Dad learned one loss can't be paid twice: insurance only indemnifies.

5.name: Sean
lines: Sean again. I've just started my first job, and I have to decide whether to join the group plan.
I can't pick my benefits, I lose them if I switch jobs, and I pay tax on premiums my employer pays. Why bother?
Dad came from England at 29 and wants to retire at 60. Can he count on OAS, CPP or government disability benefits?
Help us make sense of group plans and government programs!
5.mission: Clear Stage 5 to sort out Sean's group plan and his dad's government benefits.
5.debrief: Thanks! Group cover needs no underwriting, and taxed disability premiums mean tax-free benefits. Dad gets about 90% OAS!

6.name: Jasmine
lines: Hi, I'm Jasmine. I'm 48, single, and finally able to save seriously for retirement.
The stocks in my RRSP have had some modest success lately. What techniques could build on that?
But I won't lock every dollar away. I need to reach some of it in an emergency.
What steps should my plan follow, and where will my retirement income come from?
6.mission: Clear Stage 6 to build Jasmine a retirement plan the Inflation Titan can't crush.
6.debrief: Thanks! Set goals, size my income needs, find my sources, then max my RRSP early and use my carried-forward room.

7.name: Gitano
lines: I'm Gitano, 60, and my wife is 55. My employer pension and CPP both say I can start collecting now.
My pension offers a full amount on my life alone, or a reduced joint one that pays her two-thirds after I die.
I've also got $150,000 in an RRSP, mostly Canadian equity funds, and our $300,000 home is mortgage-free.
Should I try a reverse mortgage? I know what I can do. Help me work out what I should do!
7.mission: Clear Stage 7 so Gitano and his wife never outlive their money.
7.debrief: Thanks! A joint pension protects my wife, and at 71 an RRIF based on her younger age keeps my withdrawals low.

8.name: Angelo
lines: Angelo here. No will. When Maria and I married we owned next to nothing, and I never got around to one.
We own our house jointly. I also hold roughly $300,000 in GICs and RRSPs, and my own business is worth about $500,000.
Our sons are grown and married, and our daughter, 17, lives at home. Surely it all goes to Maria anyway... right?
Help me see what really happens to my family if I die without a will!
8.mission: Clear Stage 8 to save Angelo's family from Lord Intestate's rules.
8.debrief: Thanks! Without a will, Maria wouldn't get it all, and the kids would take their shares right away. Time for a will!

9.name: Manfred
lines: I'm Manfred, 79, and a bit forgetful lately. I picked up a do-it-yourself will kit. Would you witness it?
My son Hans insists I cut out my wife, who's in a nursing home, and make him my main beneficiary.
My brother Fritz, 71, would be executor, with my grandchildren's legacies in trust until they turn 30.
I'd give Hans power of attorney over my bank and investments. Could he touch my house or my will? Help!
9.mission: Clear Stage 9 to shield Manfred's will from the Undue Influencer.
9.debrief: Thank you! A lawyer or notary, not a kit; a younger or corporate executor; and no power of attorney can change my will.

10.name: Maureen
lines: I'm Maureen, from Ontario. I'm recently divorced, so my will needs an update.
My aunt's will was voided because she wasn't competent. How will my bank and RRSP issuers know mine is valid?
My estate is about $1,000,000, mostly real estate and securities, and I hear the fees could run to thousands.
Should I register my property jointly with my minor sons? Help me handle probate the smart way!
10.mission: Clear Stage 10 to steer Maureen through probate without a costly shortcut.
10.debrief: Thanks! Probate confirms my will is my last one. And no joint title with my boys: a trust in my will protects us all.

11.name: Maria
lines: I'm Maria. Manuel and I married in Quebec and have lived here 12 years. Now he's talking about divorce.
The house is in his name only. We have two cars, one in each name, and we gave our 16-year-old a $6,000 golf cart.
His plumbing business runs on $20,000 of tools and a $16,000 van, and half of that van came out of my pay.
On our honeymoon, at 18, he had me sign away any claim to our future home and assets. Am I stuck? Help!
11.mission: Clear Stage 11 to defend Maria's share of the family patrimony.
11.debrief: Thank you! Family patrimony can't be waived in advance, so that contract is void: the house and cars are split equally.

intro: Step right up! I'm the PRODUCT PUSHER, and have I got a product for YOU!
Goals? Plans? Bah! Buy one of everything and hope for the best!
hit: Argh! You set goals BEFORE buying?!
No! A risk analysis isn't on my price list!
Curses! Loss control AND loss financing?!
One plan beats eleven sales pitches?! Nooo!
miss: Ha! Another product for the pile!
Confused? Perfect! Buy two!
Who needs a plan when you have a brochure?
Product proliferation is my superpower!
1.defeat: Nooo! Clients want planning now, not just products... I'm obsolete!
1.win: SOLD! One more client with lots of products and no plan!

intro: I am PERIL PRIME, the cause of every loss! Fire! Theft! Collision!
And every hazard you ignore makes my odds better! Mwa-ha-ha!
hit: Argh! You moved the gasoline away from the flame!
Curses! You transferred me to an insurer!
Sprinklers?! You cut my severity!
No! You can tell a peril from a hazard!
miss: Ha! You kept that risk without even knowing it!
Uncertainty about loss? That's my whole act!
That icy road was a hazard, and you skated right in!
Low frequency, high severity, and all on you!
2.defeat: Avoided, prevented, reduced, transferred... PERIL PRIME is DOWN!
2.win: Unmanaged risk, total loss! PERIL PRIME strikes again!

intro: Wooo... I am the SOLVENCY SPECTER! I haunt every insurer's balance sheet!
Will your insurer still be there when you claim? Wooo-ha-ha-ha!
hit: Aagh! Capital requirements! They burn!
No! Assuris is guarding the policyowners!
Curses! Federal AND provincial regulators!
Eek! A licensed agent! I can't scare those!
miss: Wooo! Your confidence is going insolvent!
Stock or mutual? You'll never tell them apart!
Boo! That answer has no capital behind it!
Your reserves are looking... ghostly!
3.defeat: Regulated, capitalized and protected... I'm fading... fading... gone!
3.win: Your peace of mind just went insolvent! Wooo-ha-ha!

intro: I am THE FINE PRINT! Clauses, conditions, exclusions... all in tiny type!
Sign without reading me, and learn what all-perils does NOT cover!
hit: Argh! You used the 10-day free look!
Ambiguous wording favours the policyowner?! Nooo!
Curses! You actually read the exclusions!
Indemnity! No profiting from a loss? Rats!
miss: Ha! Didn't read the exclusions, did you?
That clause was on page 47, in six-point type!
Flood? Earthquake? Check the exclusions!
Sign here, initial there... Mwa-ha-ha!
4.defeat: Every clause read, every exclusion found... I'm null and void!
4.win: You signed without reading! The fine print wins again!

intro: I am the GROUP GOLEM, forged from one master contract and a thousand members!
Change jobs, and your group benefits stay with ME! GRAAAH!
hit: Ugh! You converted your group life in time!
Argh! You know the 40-year OAS rule!
Little or no underwriting? I'm crumbling!
Curses! My master contract is cracking!
miss: Severe AND prolonged, or no QPP disability pension!
Pick your own benefits? Not in MY group plan!
Wrong! Back to the end of the group line!
Your certificate is no match for my master contract!
5.defeat: My master contract... terminated! The group... disbands...
5.win: Absorbed into the group! Your benefits answer to ME now!

intro: I am the INFLATION TITAN! Every year I grow, and your dollars shrink!
At just 3% a year, today's $1,000 will cost $1,806 in 20 years!
hit: Argh! You used the real rate of return!
Constant dollars?! I can't touch those!
Indexed benefits! My one weakness!
Curses! You projected costs to retirement!
miss: Your purchasing power is SHRINKING!
Planning in today's dollars? How cute!
Forgot about me? I never forget you!
Your nest egg buys less every year! Ha!
6.defeat: Beaten by real rates and a solid plan... I'm deflating!
6.win: Your savings are mine! Every dollar buys less and less!

intro: I am the LONGEVITY LICH! You will live a long, long time...
...but will your money? Heh heh heh. I can wait for decades!
hit: Argh! A life annuity! You can't outlive THAT!
No! A pension that keeps paying the spouse!
Curses! An RRIF based on the younger spouse!
Ugh! You planned for a long, long life!
miss: Forgot the RRSP deadline at 71? I didn't!
Straight-life annuity with a spouse? Perfect!
Your savings will expire long before you do!
Live long... and run out of money! Mwa-ha-ha!
7.defeat: Income for life?! My curse is broken... I crumble to dust!
7.win: Your money ran out, but your years didn't! Mwa-ha-ha!

intro: Kneel before LORD INTESTATE! No will? Then the law picks your heirs!
Your spouse, your children, your estate... all split by MY rules!
hit: Argh! A valid will! My one weakness!
Curses! A named beneficiary skips my estate!
No! You chose your own liquidator!
Ugh! A trust for the minor children!
miss: Ha! The law picks your heirs now!
No will? In Quebec, a de facto spouse inherits NOTHING!
The kids' shares pay out at 18, ready or not!
Your estate, your wishes? Not without a will!
8.defeat: A valid will?! My reign... is... over...
8.win: No will, no say! Your estate now follows MY law!

intro: Psst... I'm the UNDUE INFLUENCER. Just sign where I point, friend.
A little pressure, a do-it-yourself kit, and the estate is mine!
hit: Curses! You saw the lawyer without me!
No! A sound mind AND a free will?!
Power of attorney can't change a will?! Rats!
A notary?! I can't push a notary around!
miss: Good, good... now sign right here. Trust me!
Your free will? Now it's MY will!
Shh... no need to tell your lawyer about me.
Who needs independent advice? You have ME!
9.defeat: Foiled by a sound mind and a free will! My influence is gone!
9.win: Sign here... and here... The estate is MINE! Mwa-ha-ha!

intro: PROBATRON ONLINE. Scanning will... validity UNCONFIRMED. Probate initiated!
BEEP! Assets passing through your will detected. Calculating fees...
hit: ERROR! Named beneficiary. Asset bypassed!
SYSTEM FAULT: notarial will. No probate needed!
WARNING: inter vivos gift. Asset already gone!
DOES NOT COMPUTE! A trust? Fee base shrinking!
miss: Fee meter rising! Thank you for your estate!
Holograph will detected. Probate REQUIRED. Beep!
Probated wills go public. Everyone can read it!
Joint with a minor? Control LOST! Ha-ha-beep!
10.defeat: Probate... bypassed... Estate... settled... Shutting... down...
10.win: Estate processed. Fees collected. PROBATRON thanks you. BEEP!

intro: Wooo... I am the PATRIMONY PHANTOM, haunting every Quebec marriage!
House, cars, pension rights... do you know what really gets split?
hit: Aagh! Advance waivers are null and void!
No! It's the net value that's split, not the assets!
Curses! Family cars count, in either spouse's name!
Eek! You know your partnership of acquests!
miss: Wooo! Your share is fading into the mist!
The patrimony rules are mandatory, and so is your defeat!
Lost in the matrimonial regime maze? Wooo!
Boo! You forgot what the family patrimony holds!
11.defeat: Nooo! The patrimony is split fair and square... I fade away!
11.win: Your claim vanishes into the mist! Wooo-ha-ha-ha!

intro: I am THE EXAMINATOR! Eleven chapters. One exam. Zero mercy.
Risk, contracts, retirement, wills, family law... prove you know it ALL!
hit: Impossible! You actually studied!
Argh! Correct... AGAIN!
My question bank is crumbling!
You read the follow-ups too?! Grrr!
miss: WRONG! Back to Stage 1 with you!
Ha! Did you even read the scenario?
Incorrect! The Examinator never forgets!
Was that a guess? I can always tell!
all.defeat: Impossible... You have PASSED! Go forth and plan, champion!
all.win: Exam over! Hit the books and face me again, student!
